CONCURRENT REQUIREMENTS
Before any airplane accepts the new Flight Management Computer (FMC), the airplane must have Onboard
Network System (ONS) Operating System (OS) 9.1 installed.
BACKGROUND
A review of the in-service FMC fault logs for the GE Aviation FMC has found an increase in FMC in-air restarts
due to 0x1009 fault code. The 0x1009 fault code identifies that the FMC performed a cold restart in response
to detection of a multiple bit error within the Static Random Access Memory (SRAM). A cold restart results in
the clearing of all SRAM, the loss of flight plan data and a longer restart time than a warm restart. The existing
GE Aviation FMC SRAM component was found to be more susceptible to atmospheric radiation, which leads
to an increased rate of 0x1009 fault codes. If this service bulletin is not done, airplanes with existing GE Aviation
FMCs installed can experience higher than acceptable rates of FMC in-air restarts because of SRAM multiple
bit errors caused by atmospheric radiation.
This service bulletin gives instructions to replace the existing GE Aviation FMCs with new GE Aviation FMCs.
The new FMCs use a different SRAM to decrease the possibility of FMC in-air restarts because of SRAM multiple
bit errors caused by atmospheric radiation.
Boeing Fleet Team Digest (FTD) 737MAX-FTD-34-18008 is related to this service bulletin.
Boeing Service Letter (SL) 737-SL-34-267 is related to this service bulletin.

compatible with the new FMC, part number 176200-02-01.
(h) You cannot use the existing part to replace the new or changed part.

Hardware Update
CONCURRENT REQUIREMENTS
Before any airplane accepts the new Flight Management Computer (FMC), the airplane must have Onboard
Network System (ONS) Operating System (OS) 9.1 installed.
BACKGROUND
A review of the in-service FMC fault logs for the GE Aviation FMC has found an increase in FMC in-air restarts
due to 0x1009 fault code. The 0x1009 fault code identifies that the FMC performed a cold restart in response
to detection of a multiple bit error within the Static Random Access Memory (SRAM). A cold restart results in
the clearing of all SRAM, the loss of flight plan data and a longer restart time than a warm restart. The existing
GE Aviation FMC SRAM component was found to be more susceptible to atmospheric radiation, which leads
to an increased rate of 0x1009 fault codes. If this service bulletin is not done, airplanes with existing GE Aviation
FMCs installed can experience higher than acceptable rates of FMC in-air restarts because of SRAM multiple
bit errors caused by atmospheric radiation.
This service bulletin gives instructions to replace the existing GE Aviation FMCs with new GE Aviation FMCs.
The new FMCs use a different SRAM to decrease the possibility of FMC in-air restarts because of SRAM multiple
bit errors caused by atmospheric radiation.
Boeing Fleet Team Digest (FTD) 737MAX-FTD-34-18008 is related to this service bulletin.
Boeing Service Letter (SL) 737-SL-34-267 is related to this service bulletin.
